title: Visualization, ethics and data security
text:
Prepare for the module


Prerequisites
Revisit one chart from Module 5 and one cleaning decision from Module 4. This module asks you to connect a technical output to its consequences for people represented in the data.


Minimum route
Identify one chart problem, one re-identification risk and one limit of the analysis, then propose a verifiable correction. A short, precise ethics note is better than a general promise.


CRAP and FAIR in practice
Use CRAP to review contrast, repetition, alignment and proximity in a visualization. Use FAIR to ask whether data and documentation can be found, understood and responsibly reused.


Readings and help
Start with the essential resources listed in the plan, then reserve deeper readings for review. When uncertain, do not publish potentially identifying information.

CRAP in practice
To assess a chart, explicitly check contrast, repetition, alignment and proximity. In your ethics note, name at least one visual choice that supports or harms these four principles.

title: Challenge 8 - Scraping Function
Challenge 8 - Scraping Function
text:
Minimal Robustness
The portal may display slightly different labels. Your function must therefore be able to handle at least these forms:

Organisation, Organisme, Producteur, Producer or Organization for the producer;
Catégorie, Catégories, Category or Categories for the category.

A reasonable approach is to create a small helper function that receives the text extracted from an HTML block and a search pattern, then returns the cleaned value or NA_character_.

title: Challenge 8 - Scraping Function
text:
Recommended Workflow

Work first in the console or in a draft file.
Locate dataset blocks with .dataset-content.
Extract titles with .dataset-heading a.
Locate metadata elements with .dqc-org-cat.
Build a helper function to clean labels.
Group everything in scrape_page(url).
Test the function on a local test page or on a public Données Québec page.
Place only the final required code in IDUL.R.

title: Challenge 8 - Scraping Function
Challenge 8 - Scraping Function
text:
Ethics and Server Load
For the challenge, your function must scrape one page at a time. If you later write a loop over several pages, add a pause with Sys.sleep(1) between requests.
Do not bypass protection mechanisms. Do not launch large automated collections. The robots.txt file provides a useful technical signal, but it does not replace terms of use, caution or respect for server load.

Topic Choice
Choose one option.
Option A: predictive model

title: Packages used in the course
text:
R library
  
  This page gathers the R packages used or mentioned in the notes, exercises, adventures and scripts. It explains what each package is for and where it appears in the modules.
  
  Start
  Starter block
  Choose
  Troubleshoot
  By module
  Datasets
  
  
  
  01Install once
  02Load at the start
  03Call precisely
  04Render after restart
  
  

  
  
  Working reflex
  
  A package is not just a line of code to copy: it is a dependency of your document. The useful reflex is to distinguish installation, loading and precise function calls.
  
  
  
  1
  
  install.packages("package_name") installs the package on your computer.
  
  
  2
  
  library(tidyverse) makes functions available in the active R session.
  
  
  3
  
  readr::read_csv() uses a function without loading the whole package.
  
  
  4
  
  A Quarto document must load every package it depends on inside the file itself.
  
  
  

  
  
  Reproducible report
  
  The simple rule: install in the Console when needed, load in the Quarto document, then render the document after restarting R. A submission should be rebuildable without hidden objects in the environment.
  # Start of a .qmd document
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

meteo <- UlavalSSD::MeteoQuebec
  
  
  Use install.packages() or a GitHub installation instruction when the package is not installed yet.
  Put the required library() calls inside the .qmd file, ideally near the beginning.
  Use package::function() when only one function is needed or when a name may conflict.
  Restart R, render the document, then check that every dependency is visible in the submitted file.
  
  

  
  
  Choose the tool
  
  The modules often return to the same families of tasks. This map helps you pick the right tool before opening the detailed documentation.
  
  
  
  
  readr, readxl, jsonlite, haven
  
  
  
  dplyr, tidyr, stringr, forcats, lubridate
  
  
  
  ggplot2, patchwork, scales, viridis, ggcorrplot
  
  
  
  UlavalSSD, palmerpenguins, nycflights23, gapminder, Lahman
  
  
  
  rvest, robotstxt, purrr, stringr
  
  
  
  tidytext, stopwords, plotly, flexdashboard, shiny
  
  
  

  
  
  Troubleshooting
  
  Most package errors come from one of the four situations below.
  
  
  
  
  Install the package, then render the document again. Installation is done once per computer.
  
  
  
  Load the package with library() or call the function with package::function().
  
  
  
  Use an explicit call, such as dplyr::filter(), to tell R which function to use.
  
  
  
  Add the required library() calls inside the .qmd file, not only in the Console.

title: Session project
text:
Integrative assessment
  Session project
  The project turns the skills practised in the modules into a complete analysis: choose a question, document data, build a reproducible workflow and communicate a useful result.
  
  Full statement
  Assessments
  Data sources
  Before each milestone
  
  
  
  15Proposal
  45Presentation
  15Final summary
  25Repository and team
  
  

  
  
  Work path
  Dates and administrative requirements are confirmed on Brio. The site explains the project logic and the expected products.
  
  
  1ProposalStabilize the question, data source and analysis plan in proposition/proposition.qmd.
  2DevelopmentPrepare data, structure scripts and keep a clear trace of decisions in GitHub.
  3PresentationPresent results in 15 minutes with presentation/presentation.qmd.
  4Final summaryTurn the repository README.md into a clear project synthesis.
  
  

  
  
  Allowed AI Use
  In challenges and the project, AI is allowed as support for reasoning, debugging, revision, planning or checking. In the exam, only the tools explicitly authorized on Brio are allowed. In all cases, the final deliverable must remain verifiable, personal and consistent with the instructions. You must understand, test and be able to explain any submitted code, text, source, result or interpretation. When AI influences an important part of an evaluated deliverable, keep a short trace: tool used, purpose of help, affected part and verification done. The official requirements posted on Brio always prevail.
  
  

  
  
  Before each milestone
  Each project submission should be readable by someone who opens the repository without hearing you explain it.
  
  Check the date, submission location and expected file on Brio.
  Render the relevant Quarto documents and open the produced HTML files.
  Check that the GitHub repository contains useful files and no temporary files.
  Reread the question, data, results and limitations as an external reader.
  Make sure team contributions are visible and coherent.
  
  
  
  ProposalQuestion, data and analysis plan stabilized.
  PresentationMain results, central visualization and limitations.
  Final summaryStandalone README, useful links and reproducibility traces.
  
  

  
  
  What the project assesses
  The project is more open than the challenges. It assesses your ability to make reasoned choices and make them readable.
  
  
  QuestionFormulate a problem precise enough to guide the analysis.
  DataDescribe source, variables, limitations and important transformations.
  AnalysisUse course tools to explore, visualize, compare and interpret.
  CommunicationMake the work understandable for someone discovering the project.
  
  

  
  
  Data and responsibility
  The project asks for real autonomy, but that autonomy comes with responsibility for provenance, rights and data protection.
  
  
  ProvenanceThe source must be identifiable, cited and stable enough to be found again.
  Usage rightsThe license or terms should allow use in the course context.
  Sensitive dataUnnecessary personal or identifying information should not be shared in a public repository.
  LimitationsBiases, missing values, filters and important transformations must be explained.
  
  

  
  
  GitHub template
  The project template provides the starting structure: data, scripts, Quarto proposal, Quarto presentation and final summary in the README.
  
  Read the statement
  Open the template
  Toolbox
  
  
  
  Start simpleA clear, well-treated question is better than an overly broad project.
  Commit oftenThe repository should show a progressive and reproducible process.
  Reread as a readerThe final product should be understandable without extra oral explanation.

      STT-1100 Resources
      This page helps you find the right support at the right moment: reading before a module, working through an adventure, practising with exercises, finding a function, choosing a dataset, asking for help or preparing a submission.

      What am I looking for?
      Start from your situation. The site has many resources; the goal is to reduce noise.
    
    
      
        I am preparing a module
        Return to the learning plan, read the targeted references, then complete the formative mini-test.
        
          Module overviewFind the module and its learning plan.
          Books and readingsOpen the relevant chapters and guides.
        
      
      
        I am stuck on code
        Identify the error, reduce the example, compare with a course routine, then ask for targeted help.
        
          ToolkitR, Quarto, GitHub and troubleshooting routines.
          AI and helpUse STT-1100 GPT while staying in control.
        
      
      
        I am looking for data
        Find local files, package datasets and datasets useful for exercises.
        
          DatasetsCatalog by module and file profiles.
          R packagesSee which packages provide data or functions.
        
      
      
        I am preparing a submission
        Reread the instructions, check the expected format, render the document and remove unnecessary files.
        
          ChallengesRole, formats and links to instructions.
          EvaluationsUnderstand what is valued in deliverables.
        
      
      
        I want more practice
        Use the independent exercises to redo module moves in another context and with other data.

        I am preparing the project
        Return to project expectations, choose targeted resources and keep a reproducible trace of decisions.
        
          Session projectConsult the structure, milestones and deliverables.
          Books and readingsFind useful references for deepening a method.
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Where am I in the module?
      A module is not just a list of pages. Each resource plays a different role depending on the moment of work.
    
    
      
        Before the module
        Read the learning plan, open the essential readings and identify the data that will return during the week.
        
          ModulesStart from the current module page.
          ReadingsConsult only the targeted references.
        
      
      
        During the adventure
        Follow the narrative, produce code in the Quarto document and check intermediate outputs often.
        
          ToolkitFind recurring technical moves.
          Class supportsOpen cheat sheets and practical guides.
        
      
      
        After the adventure
        Use exercises as independent consolidation. They help you practise, not continue the challenge by default.
        
          Exercises by moduleExercises are available from each module.
          Exercise dataCompare contexts and available files.
        
      
      
        Before submitting
        Reread the official instructions, render the document, check the files and submit according to Brio instructions.
        
          ChallengesFind instructions and expected formats.
          EvaluationsUnderstand the role of each production.
        
      
    
  

  
    
      Specialized Pages
      These pages contain the details. This page mainly helps you choose where to go.
    
    
      
        
        Books and Readings

        Class Supports
        Cheat sheets, presentations, practical guides and complementary material.
        Open supports
      
      
        
        AI and Help
        Use the course AI to review, debug and improve reasoning while staying in control. Example request: Review my reasoning, indicate what is supported by the data and what still needs checking.
        Open AI help

        Toolkit
        R functions, Quarto, GitHub, troubleshooting routines and recurring course gestures.
        Open toolkit
      
    
  

  
    
      Work Method
      Resources are more useful when they are used in the right order.
    
    
      1LocateStart from the module page, then identify readings, data, packages and expected productions.
      2WorkMove through the adventure or exercise, test code often and keep a clear trace in Quarto.
      3UnblockReduce the problem, read the error, consult the toolkit, then ask for targeted help when needed.
      4CheckRender the document, reread results, check links, then return to the instructions before submitting.
    
  

  
    
      Two Landmarks to Keep
      Resources help you learn and work. They never replace the specific instructions for a challenge, exam, project or the official conditions listed on Brio.

      Instructions FirstBefore a submission, reread the expected product, requested files and submission location.
      Targeted ResourceChoose the page that answers the immediate need instead of opening the whole site.
      Verifiable TraceWhen a resource changes your work, rerun the code, reread the text and keep a clear version.
